question.text: An excess of <math><msub><mrow><mtext>AgNO</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi></math> solution is added to <math><mn>100</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> of a <math><mn>0.2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi></math> dichloridotetraaquachromium <math><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">III</mi><mo>)</mo></math> chloride. The number of millimoles of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></math> precipitated would be -----.

solution.text:
100mL of 0.2M solution means 0.02 moles of complex ∵1001000×0.2=0.02
CrH2O4Cl2Cl has one ionizable Cl-.
∴0.02 moles of the complex precipitates the same amount of AgCl .
∴ Millimoles of AgCl precipitated =20
